steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Alright, let's continue.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The Infected and Non-Infected stand equal in prison. Now isn't that the picture of irony.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...You can't call that equal.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Keheh. You're right. If we have to suffer inhumanity to reach equality, then that's probably an equal we shouldn't want.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Can we change the subject?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I wasn't planning on continuing this one. Chat about this stuff from all lofty up high and you'll sleep terrible at night.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Alright. Kafka went inside... four and a half months ago? The break happened four months ago, right while Mansfield State Prison was stopped over at San Sophie City.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Of course, any earlier, and we'd have to go a year back.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: After all, as a nomadic prison, it'd only visit cities on the periphery once every few months to restock and take in new inmates. The rest of the time, it stopped in the middle of the barrens.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Four months to plot a jailbreak. Can't say that's short, but I can't say it's that long either.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hm? Wait, actually, that gives me a question.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: By the rules you gave, it should be my turn to ask.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Ahahah, right, yeah. Go ahead, then.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...Before that, Mayer, could I ask you to make something for us to eat?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Huh? Yeah, sure. But I don't know if I can use the kitchen in here, so.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You can use it! I thought this chat'd probably take ages, so I actually prepped a whole bunch of ingredients.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Can you cook, Ms. Mayer?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Sure I can cook. I'm a solo workshop. If I couldn't make grub, I woulda starved to death forever ago.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I mean, Rhine Lab and Rhodes Island both have cafeterias, but sometimes it's just a pain in the ass to walk over, y'know?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: You keep talking. I'll go make you some eats.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Make sure you examine those ingredients, right? I don't wanna get accused of fiddling with your food here.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Ayo~

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You are so... hospitable.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Keheh. I told you! I came to chat with you.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Can't dodge me. Why'd you get Mayer out of the picture?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...Because I still haven't told her that Energy are behind HydeBro.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Wait, don't tell me you didn't plot this together?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No. I wouldn't tell her in the first place. She only came with me to procure equipment.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So that's how it is. I see, 'cause Energy and Engineering walk pretty close. You wouldn't wanna sour her outlook.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But given she wasn't your partner-in-crime, would you run that much risk telling her?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...I don't need you to remind me.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Set it aside. What I want to know is: During all of this, what was Energy's position like?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: They were backing HydeBro, but had nothing to do with the business itself.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It was HydeBro who tapped Energy's resources to cook up their assassination plot.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I see, then.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Alright. My turn to ask, then—

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: As far as I know, Anthony's accomplices in the jailbreak included the prison's original mortician, Ms. Domma, but also a woman by the name of Robin.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: What bugs me about that is, by my intel, Robin should've been one of the assassins sent to take Anthony out.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But going by your version of the events, you seem to have just one helper, and that's Ms. Kafka.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Could it be Robin wasn't your doing?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...It appears you have no idea how the jailbreak went, Director Muelsyse.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I said that already.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: On top of that, you've gotten one thing wrong. I had no immediate knowledge that this assassination would take place.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Whuh?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: If I had any awareness of it beforehand, I wouldn't have had Kafka infiltrate the prison alone.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It was far too dangerous for her. And under those circumstances, what she could accomplish was very limited.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Wait, you're not telling me you only got Anthony?! He's your only lead?!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I am. I only realized in the past half year that Anthony was not incarcerated in the same prison as the rest of his family. Following that, I arranged for Kafka to make her way in.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: My thought process at the time was: If she could meet him and help him break out of jail, perfect. If she couldn't, then oh well.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: ...And then you managed to bump straight into the whole assassination.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Oh, the pieces are fitting... This makes so much actual sense.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But... are you sure you should've told me about this?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: If you'd kept me going like you were gonna stop the assassination, I'd have been way more impressed, you know.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm no expert at that sort of thing, Director Muelsyse.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I see. At first, I thought we were alike, but looking at it now, it's Ms. Mayer. That's who you're like. You're the same sort of person.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But you have the research you love, and you don't care about much else. So there's gotta be some reason you were forced to care about this.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: And that reason, I'm guessing, is the 'Diαbolic Crisis,' right?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That and this are unrelated matters, Director Muelsyse.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: If you came to talk about Ifrit, then our conversation ends here.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sorry, sorry. Should've kept my mouth shut. It's okay, I've only heard things about it. I don't even know what happened.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: As a token of apology, I'll give you a free question.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...You needn't.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What I require isn't your apology. I require you to never bring it up again. That will do.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Got it. Then let's just continue where we left off.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...Remember, as far as I'm concerned, this assassination was completely unaccounted for. I didn't imagine HydeBro would do things that way.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Well. That goes to show you don't have a full grasp on Energy's MO.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Anthony's a hidden danger. Imagine some entity that can't allow any hidden danger or uncontrollable elements. Imagine they find out they've left a little loose end...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: That's the end of the Bros.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So they've spent a couple years weaving this hit together. Making it real. Burying an imprisoned Anthony six feet under.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...To cover up their evil, they cannot help but do more evil.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It makes me retch.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But there are some things that can't be walked back, huh?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Back to the assassin, by the way. If that woman, Robin, wasn't backed by you, then that only leaves one possibility.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Robin's an assassin who went turncoat midway. Right?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So, could I trouble you to switch angles? I'm a little curious about this assassin lady and her prisonly actions.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Given she and Anthony escaped together, I'm sure you've verified her status and experiences yourself?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Robin... was, true enough, initially one assassin dispatched to the prison to take Anthony out.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Around the time Kafka recalled that clash between the prisoners, she hadn't been in there for too long.
